sourcedFrom: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") (undated beyond "V26.1" on the back page)
cleanIntro:
The PWS BDE36-Ti is a modular titanium rifle can, rated up to .338 Lapua Magnum on a barrel of 20 inches or more, and full-auto rated. Its entrance chamber and main baffle stack are 3D-printed titanium; four CNC-turned modular baffles and a flat end cap thread on in front, and the exterior is DLC coated. It ships with a removable 5/8-24 direct-thread mount, and the entrance chamber also threads onto a 1.375-24 (HUB) mount.

The routine never opens the can: it comes off the host, you look through the bore, clean the outside with a nylon brush and CLP, and check that everything is tight. Deep Clean is PWS's own separation with the two supplied wrenches, every part brushed or soaked in CLP, and the can put back together exactly as it came apart. PWS recommends cleaning, lubricating and checking torque every 500 rounds.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, host cleared by its own manual
steps.action: Point the host's muzzle in a safe direction and keep it there. Clear the host firearm by its own manual before your hands go near the can: this book teaches the suppressor and prints no clearing procedure for any host.
steps.prose: Your hand is about to be wrapped around the muzzle end. Treat the gun as loaded until you have seen it empty.
steps.quote: ALWAYS KEEP THE MUZZLE OF A FIREARM POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION REGARDLESS OF WHETHER THE FIREARM IS LOADED.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Warnings, item 1, p.6
steps.warn: TREAT ALL FIREARMS AS LOADED AT ALL TIMES.

steps.title: Rated up to .338 Lapua Mag, 20-inch barrel minimum
steps.action: Before going further, check what this can has been fed and on what barrel. PWS rates the BDE 36 up to .338 Lapua Magnum, with a minimum barrel length of 20 inches. Nothing bigger, and no shorter barrel at that rating.
steps.prose: PWS warns that the wrong ammunition can jam, fail to fire or build excessive pressure.
steps.quote: THE BDE® 36 IS RATED UP TO 338 LAPUA MAG WITH A MINIMUM 20 INCH BARREL LENGTH
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Specifications, Restrictions, p.8

steps.title: Let it cool before you touch it
steps.action: Do not handle the can hot. Let the firearm and the suppressor cool completely before you touch either, and set it down where it touches nothing while it cools.
steps.prose: PWS: a suppressor gets far hotter than the 140°F skin-burn limit, and a hot can does not look hot.
steps.caution: Suppressor can cause burn, damage, or destroy anything it touches; ensure your suppressor is not in contact with anything while it cools.
steps.quote: Do not handle a hot suppressor. Allow the firearm and suppressor to completely cool prior to any contact.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Warnings, Suppressors Get Hot, p.4

steps.title: Can off the host
steps.action: Unscrew the can from the host. On the supplied mount it comes off the host's 5/8-24 muzzle threads; on a 1.375-24 (HUB) mount the entrance chamber unthreads from the mount. PWS's book prints no removal procedure for the host. If it is carbon-locked, do not force it.
steps.prose: Note how tight it was when it came off: it tells you whether it was staying put.
steps.quote: Your BDE® ships with a 5/8-24 thread adapter, so you can directly thread the BDE® to your platform of choice.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Mounting Options, Direct Thread, p.13

steps.title: Look through the bore
steps.action: Look through the can from end to end for anything blocking the bore, including mud or sand.
steps.prose: An obstruction in the bore of a suppressor is something a bullet will find.
steps.quote: Visually inspect the suppressor for any bore obstructions including natural matter like mud and/or sand.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Maintenance, p.14

steps.title: Nylon brush and CLP on the outside
steps.action: Clean the outside of the can with a nylon brush and a CLP-type product. The exterior is DLC coated, so some cleaners and solvents must not be used on it. Wear gloves and safety goggles, and work in a well-ventilated place away from open flame.
steps.prose: PWS warns that cleaning a suppressor carries potential toxicity.
steps.caution: Please be aware that the exterior is DLC (Diamond-like carbon) coated, so certain cleaners and solvents should not be used.
steps.quote: To clean any part of this assembly, use a nylon brush with CLP (Cleaner, Lubricant, Preservative) type of product.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Maintenance, p.14
steps.warn: When cleaning a suppressor, you should wear gloves and safety goggles.

steps.title: Every part tight
steps.action: Check that every part of the can is tight, and check the torque at least every 500 rounds. PWS warns that a can left unchecked can cause baffle strikes and damage the suppressor and the firearm.
steps.prose: PWS ties this to accuracy: a loose part is a can out of line.
steps.quote: Regular tightening should be done on all parts of the suppressor to ensure accuracy is maintained.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Maintenance, p.14
steps.warn: WE RECOMMEND CHECKING TORQUE SPECS EVERY 500 ROUNDS MINIMUM.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The can is off the host, cool, its bore inspected, its outside clean and every part checked tight. That is the routine. Deep Clean is PWS's own separation with the two supplied wrenches, every part cleaned, and the can rebuilt as it came apart.
steps.prose: PWS recommends cleaning, lubricating and checking torque every 500 rounds.
steps.quote: Your PWS BDE® Suppressor should be routinely checked and maintained for preventative measures.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Maintenance, p.14

deepSteps.title: The two supplied wrenches separate every part
deepSteps.action: Take the two wrenches that came with the can. PWS separates each part of the assembly with them, with the parts diagram in front of you. Lay the parts out in the order they come off, so the can goes back together exactly as it was.
deepSteps.prose: PWS's parts diagram names them: the 5/8-24 thread mount, the entrance chamber, the main baffle stack, the four modular baffles and the flat end cap. PWS prints this separation under its modifications heading; here it is used only to clean, and nothing is left out or moved when it goes back.
deepSteps.quote: To modify the BDE® 36, simply use the 2 supplied wrenches to seperate each part of the assembly.
deepSteps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Modifications, p.11

deepSteps.title: Wrench notch on the outside, a cloth under it
deepSteps.action: Seat the small notch on the large side of the wrench on the outside of the can, and make sure it is securely aligned before you turn. A thin cloth between the wrench and the can protects the finish.
deepSteps.prose: A wrench that slips scratches the DLC coating.
deepSteps.caution: Ensure that the wrench is securely aligned to avoid scratches to the surface finish.
deepSteps.quote: The large side of the wrench has a small notch which aligns to the exterior of the suppressor.
deepSteps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Modifications, p.11

deepSteps.title: One wrench against the other
deepSteps.action: Use the two wrenches in opposite directions, one holding and one turning, to break each joint loose.
deepSteps.prose: Carbon locks threads together; two wrenches turn the joint without twisting the rest of the can.
deepSteps.quote: The supplied wrenches can be used in opposite directions to make disassembly and reassembly easier.
deepSteps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Modifications, p.12

deepSteps.title: Each part stays whole — PWS's stopping point
deepSteps.action: Stop here. On the bench: thread mount, entrance chamber, main baffle stack, the modular baffles and the end cap. None of them is taken apart, adjusted or changed.
deepSteps.prose: PWS's separation ends at the parts in its parts diagram.
deepSteps.quote: NEVER MANIPULATE, ADJUST, OR CHANGE ANY OF THE INTERNAL COMPONENTS OF YOUR FIREARM AND/OR SUPPRESSOR.
deepSteps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Warnings, item 10, p.6

deepSteps.title: Nylon brush and CLP on every part
deepSteps.action: Clean each part with a nylon brush and a CLP-type product. Keep cleaners and solvents that are not safe on DLC away from the outside of the can. Gloves and safety goggles, in a well-ventilated place away from open flame.
deepSteps.caution: Please be aware that the exterior is DLC (Diamond-like carbon) coated, so certain cleaners and solvents should not be used.
deepSteps.quote: To clean any part of this assembly, use a nylon brush with CLP (Cleaner, Lubricant, Preservative) type of product.
deepSteps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Maintenance, p.14
deepSteps.warn: When cleaning a suppressor, you should wear gloves and safety goggles.

deepSteps.title: Soak for stuck-on carbon
deepSteps.action: Carbon that the brush will not shift: soak the individual parts in CLP, then brush again.
deepSteps.prose: Soak the parts, not the whole can.
deepSteps.quote: You can soak individual parts in CLP for any stuck-on carbon.
deepSteps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE36-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE36-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Maintenance, p.14

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & BORE
tasks: Interval: clean, lubricate and check torque every 500 rounds
Look through the bore for obstructions, mud and sand included
Nylon brush and CLP on the outside
⚠ The exterior is DLC coated: some cleaners and solvents must not be used on it
Gloves and safety goggles, well-ventilated, away from open flame

cleaning.name: THREADS & TIGHTNESS
tasks: Every part of the can tight
Torque checked at least every 500 rounds
Oil or grease on the threads before it goes back on

cleaning.name: DEEP CLEAN: BAFFLES, STACK, CAPS
tasks: Deep clean: nylon brush and CLP on the end cap, modular baffles, main baffle stack, entrance chamber and mount
Deep clean: soak individual parts in CLP for stuck-on carbon
Do not manipulate, adjust or change the internal components: every part stays whole
⚠ Never thread a modular baffle or the end cap directly onto the entrance chamber: the thread pitch is different

reassembly: Oil or grease on the threads of every part, to stop carbon locking them together.
Put the parts back in the order they came off, every modular baffle back in its place: this guide rebuilds the can in the configuration it came apart in.
Never thread a modular baffle or the end cap directly onto the entrance chamber. PWS warns the thread pitch is different and it will damage the threads on the suppressor and its parts.
Turn each joint with the two supplied wrenches in opposite directions, the notch securely aligned on the outside of the can and a thin cloth under the wrench to protect the finish.

Torque: PWS's torque specifications call for a 3/8" torque wrench, all parts to 25 ft. lbs. and the thread mount to the entrance chamber to 30 ft. lbs. Do not overtighten. PWS's maintenance warning prints a different figure, 7 ft. lb., and the book does not reconcile the two: if you are unsure which applies, ask PWS before you torque.
Thread the can back onto the host, threads oiled or greased, and check its fit and retention: all hardware tightened and properly fit.
fncheck: PWS's book publishes no function check. With the host unloaded and cleared, look through the bore with the can mounted: nothing may block the bullet's path. Check that the can is tight on the host and that all hardware is tightened and properly fit; PWS puts checking fit and retention on the owner before every use. If the can is worn, loose or ill-fitting to the host, stop using it.
